1.title: Information Protection, Data Lifecycle and Governance
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Information Protection, Data Lifecycle and Governance. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Describe data classification capabilities. Describe the value of content explorer and activity explorer. Describe sensitivity labels and sensitivity label policies. Describe data loss prevention (D L P). Describe records management. Describe retention policies, retention labels and retention label policies. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions (twenty to twenty-five percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: The data protection journey
1.text: The data protection journey. Microsoft Purview protects data in four steps: know it, protect it, prevent loss, and govern it over time. Know your data. Data classification, content explorer, activity explorer. Protect your data. Sensitivity labels and policies, encryption. Prevent data loss. Data loss prevention (D L P). Govern your data. Retention, records management.

1.title: The data protection journey, continued
1.text: The data protection journey. The figure shows this: Know, protect, prevent loss and govern: the Purview data protection journey.

1.title: Data classification
1.text: Data classification. Data classification finds and labels data by type and sensitivity. Sensitive information types (S I Ts). Patterns such as credit card or national I D numbers, using patterns, keywords and checksums. Trainable classifiers. Machine learning models that learn what a document type looks like (for example contracts). Exact data match (E D M). Match against your own sensitive data in a table. Exam tip: Credit card numbers equals sensitive information type. "Documents that look like resumes or contracts" equals trainable classifier.

1.title: Content explorer and activity explorer
1.text: Content explorer and activity explorer. Content explorer. Shows: The actual items (files, emails) that carry sensitivity labels, retention labels or sensitive info types, with their location and content. Question: What is labeled, and where is it? Activity explorer. Shows: What happened to labeled content: label changes, file copies, shares, D L P matches over time. Question: What activity is occurring?

1.title: Content explorer and activity explorer, continued
1.text: Content explorer and activity explorer. The figure shows this: Content explorer lists labeled items; activity explorer shows actions taken on them. Exam tip: Content explorer equals the "what and where". Activity explorer equals the "who did what and when". Both are in the Purview portal and need appropriate roles.

1.title: Sensitivity labels and policies
1.text: Sensitivity labels and policies. A sensitivity label is a tag that classifies and protects a file or email. The label travels with the content. Encryption. Only named people can open the file. Content marking. Header, footer, watermark such as "Confidential". Access restrictions. Control who can copy, print, forward. Scope. Files, emails, Teams, Share Point sites and groups, and more.

1.title: Sensitivity labels and policies, continued
1.text: Sensitivity labels and policies. Sensitivity label. The tag and its protections. Sensitivity label policy. Publishes labels to chosen users or groups and sets rules such as mandatory labeling, default label and justification for downgrade.

1.title: Sensitivity labels and policies, continued
1.text: Sensitivity labels and policies. The figure shows this: A label policy publishes sensitivity labels to users, who apply them to files and email.

1.title: Sensitivity labels and policies, continued
1.text: Sensitivity labels and policies. Labels can be applied manually by users or automatically when content matches a sensitive information type. Exam tip: Label equals the tag and protection. Label policy equals who gets which labels and the rules for using them. A label does nothing for a user until it is published in a policy.

1.title: Data loss prevention (DLP)
1.text: Data loss prevention (D L P). D L P identifies, monitors and protects sensitive information to stop it leaving the organization by accident or on purpose. Locations. Exchange email, Share Point, One Drive, Teams, Windows and mac O S endpoints, and more. Conditions. Content contains a sensitive info type, a label, or is shared externally. Actions. Block, warn (policy tip with override), audit only, notify. Tips. Policy tips teach users why an action is risky. Example: block email that contains a credit card number sent to an external address, and notify the sender. Exam tip: D L P equals prevent sensitive data from leaving (email, share, copy to U S B). Sensitivity labels equals classify and protect the content. They work together.

1.title: Retention and records management
1.text: Retention and records management. Data lifecycle management keeps what you need and removes what you do not. Retention policy. Applies broadly to locations (all mailboxes, a site) to retain, delete, or retain then delete. Retention label. Applied to individual items; the label travels with the item and can start retention from an event or declare a record. Retention label policy. Publishes retention labels to users or applies them automatically. Records management. Marks items as records or regulatory records so they are immutable (cannot be edited or deleted by users), with file plan, disposition review and proof of disposal. Whichever retain rule applies, the item is kept; retention wins over deletion if both apply.

1.title: Retention and records management, continued
1.text: Retention and records management. The figure shows this: Retention policy applies broadly; retention labels apply per item; records are locked. Exam tip: Policy equals broad, location-based. Label equals per item and follows the file. Record equals locked so it cannot be changed or deleted. Retention label policy equals how labels are published to users.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to stop emails containing credit card numbers from being sent externally. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Data loss prevention. D L P can block or warn on sensitive information leaving the organization.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which tool shows the actual files that have a particular sensitivity label and where they are stored? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Content explorer. Content explorer lists labeled items and their locations.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An admin wants to see how many times labeled files were copied or shared last month. Which tool? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Activity explorer. Activity explorer shows actions taken on labeled content over time.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. What makes sensitivity labels available to chosen users? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A sensitivity label policy. Label policies publish labels to users or groups.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company wants to keep all Exchange mailboxes for seven years, then delete. Which tool fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A retention policy. Retention policies apply broadly to locations to retain and delete.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What does declaring an item a record do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Locks it so it cannot be edited or deleted by users. Records are immutable under records management.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the three classifier types. Answer: Sensitive information types, trainable classifiers and exact data match. Question two. What does a sensitivity label do? Answer: Classifies and protects content with encryption, markings and access limits. Question three. What does D L P stand for? Answer: Data loss prevention.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the difference between a retention policy and label? Answer: A policy applies broadly to locations; a label applies to individual items. Question five. What is a regulatory record? Answer: A stricter record that nobody can alter or remove, including administrators. Question six. Which explorer shows activity over time? Answer: Activity explorer.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Classification: sensitive information types, trainable classifiers, exact data match. Explorers: content explorer equals what and where; activity explorer equals what happened. Sensitivity labels: encryption, markings, access limits; label policy publishes them. D L P: blocks or warns on sensitive data leaving; email, Share Point, One Drive, Teams, endpoints. Retention and records: retention policy broad; retention label per item and publishes via label policy. In the next module, we continue the course.
